text_blocks.snippet: Spinal degeneration, often referred to as degenerative disc disease, can cause a variety of symptoms, with pain and nerve-related issues being the most common. Symptoms vary depending on the location and severity of the degeneration, but generally include back or neck pain, numbness, tingling, and weakness in the arms or legs. In more severe cases, nerve compression can lead to difficulty walking and even loss of bladder or bowel control.
